passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The following discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements based on current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risks and uncertainties, which could cause our actual results to differ materially from those anticipated or implied by any forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause or contribute to such differences include, but are not limited to, those discussed in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, and in particular, the risks discussed under the caption “Risk Factors” in Part I, Item 1A of this report. Our Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (“MD&A”) is organized as follows: • Overview. A discussion of our business and overall analysis of financial and other highlights in order to provide context for the remainder of MD&A. • Key Financial Metrics. A summary of our U.S. GAAP and non-GAAP key financial metrics, which management monitors to evaluate our performance. • Results of Operations. A discussion of the nature and trends in our financial results and an analysis of our financial results comparing fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2025. For discussion and analysis related to our financial results comparing fiscal 2025 to 2024, refer to Part II, Item 7 Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal 2025, which was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on August 29, 2025. • Liquidity and Capital Resources. An analysis of changes on our balance sheets and cash flows, and a discussion of our financial condition and our ability to meet cash needs. • Critical Accounting Estimates. A discussion of our accounting policies that require critical estimates, assumptions, and judgments. • Recent Accounting Pronouncements. A discussion of expected impacts of impending accounting changes on financial information to be reported in the future. Overview Our mission is to be the cybersecurity partner of choice, protecting our digital way of life. Our platforms and services help secure enterprise users, networks, clouds, endpoints, AI apps and agents, and identities by delivering comprehensive cybersecurity backed by AI and automation, and provide real-time visibility and monitoring across cloud infrastructure, applications and AI workloads. A key element of our strategy is to help our customers simplify their security architectures through consolidating disparate point products. We execute on this strategy by developing our capabilities and packaging our offerings into platforms, which are able to cover many of our customers’ needs in the markets in which we operate. Our platformization strategy combines various products and services into a tightly integrated architecture for more secure, faster, and cost-effective outcomes. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties including those described below. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties that we are unaware of, or that we currently believe are not material, also may become important factors that affect us. If any of the following risks or others not specified below materialize, our business, financial condition, and operating results could be materially adversely affected, and the market price of our common stock could decline. In addition, the impacts of any worsening of the economic environment may exacerbate the risks described below, any of which could have a material impact on us. Risk Factor Summary Our business is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties. These risks include, but are not limited to, the following: • Our operating results may be adversely affected by unfavorable economic and market conditions and the uncertain geopolitical environment. • Our business and operations have experienced growth in recent periods, and if we do not effectively manage our future growth or are unable to improve our systems, processes, and controls, our business and operating results could be adversely affected. • Our revenue growth rate in recent periods may not be indicative of our future performance, and we may not be able to maintain profitability, which could cause our business, financial condition, and operating results to suffer. • Our operating results may vary significantly from period to period, including due to seasonality, which makes our results difficult to predict and could cause our results to fall short of expectations. • If we are unable to sell new and additional products, subscriptions, and support offerings to existing end-customers or attract new customers, especially large enterprise customers, our future revenue and operating results will be harmed. • We rely on revenue from subscription and support offerings, and because we recognize revenue from subscription and support over the term of the relevant service period, downturns or upturns in sales or renewals of these subscription and support offerings are not immediately reflected in full in our operating results. • Our consumption- or usage-based offerings may expose us to customer usage optimization behavior that could create revenue volatility. • The sales prices of our products, subscriptions, and support offerings may decrease, which may reduce our revenue and gross profits and adversely impact our financial results. • We rely on our channel partners to sell a substantial portion of our products, including subscriptions and support, and if these channel partners fail to perform, our ability to sell and distribute our products and subscriptions will be limited and our operating results will be harmed. • We are exposed to the credit and liquidity risk of our customers, and to credit exposure in weakened markets, credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow covers debt service comfortably, with free cash flow after capital spending exceeding total debt by a wide margin. This cash generation reflects a subscription-heavy cybersecurity franchise whose platformization strategy drives recurring revenue and high renewal visibility, supporting a minimal indicative financial risk profile and ample headroom against sector leverage norms.

The balance sheet carries net cash, as cash and short-term investments exceed convertible notes outstanding. Gross leverage sits below the sector median, and net leverage is negative, placing the issuer in the strongest tier of the indicative risk framework. Liquidity is further supported by substantial cash balances relative to near-term obligations.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage flags reliance on channel partners for a substantial portion of product and subscription sales, plus customer credit and liquidity exposure in weakened markets. Any partner failure or customer default could disrupt distribution and collections, pressuring revenue and cash conversion even though current operating cash flow remains robust.

Debt consists of convertible notes, a structure that may require refinancing or settlement at maturity. The debt maturity schedule is not disclosed in the bundle, and the debt figure is a partial instrument-tag sum that may omit facilities. This limits visibility into refinancing needs, though net cash and strong free cash flow mitigate near-term concern.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow covers convertible notes outstanding multiple times over, and operating cash flow is similarly strong. With cash exceeding debt, the issuer could retire the notes from balance-sheet resources. Interest expense is reported as zero, so conventional coverage is not meaningful; this data gap is immaterial given the net cash position.

Cash uses include buybacks and acquisitions, which absorb a meaningful share of free cash flow. Even after these outflows, internally generated funds remain sufficient to service debt. The current ratio sits below the sector median, reflecting heavy deferred revenue and other current liabilities rather than liquidity strain, in our judgement.

overall_credit_view.text: We view the credit profile as strong, supported by net cash, robust free cash flow and leverage below the sector median. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal. Operating margin trails the sector median, and operating income declined from the prior year, so profitability trends warrant monitoring even as revenue growth outpaces the sector.

Our forward view is that debt service capacity remains ample, with free cash flow and cash balances covering convertible notes. Acquisitions and buybacks consume most free cash flow, and convertible note maturity timing is undisclosed. We would monitor refinancing plans and profitability recovery; the indicative profile is not a rating.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋債務償付，資本開支後的自由現金流大幅超過總債務。此現金產生能力反映一間以訂閱為主導的網絡安全企業，其平台化策略帶動經常性收入及高度續約可見度，支持最低的指示性財務風險狀況，並相對行業槓桿常態擁有充裕緩衝。
資產負債表持有淨現金，因現金及短期投資超過未償還可換股票據。總槓桿低於行業中位數，淨槓桿為負，使發行人處於指示性風險框架中最強級別。流動性進一步受到相對短期債務的龐大現金結餘支持。

key_risks.text: 風險因素章節指出，產品及訂閱銷售有相當部分依賴渠道合作夥伴，加上在疲弱市場中的客戶信貸及流動性風險。任何合作夥伴失敗或客戶違約均可擾亂分銷及收款，對收入及現金轉換構成壓力，儘管目前營運現金流仍然穩健。
債務由可換股票據組成，該結構可能需要在到期時再融資或結算。債務到期時間表未在資料匯編中披露，而債務數字為部分工具標籤總和，可能遺漏融資安排。此限制對再融資需求的可見度，儘管淨現金及強勁自由現金流緩解近期憂慮。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流覆蓋未償還可換股票據多倍，營運現金流同樣強勁。由於現金超過債務，發行人可從資產負債表資源清還票據。利息開支報告為零，故傳統覆蓋率不具意義；鑑於淨現金狀況，此數據缺口並不重大。
現金用途包括回購及收購，佔自由現金流相當比例。即使計及該等流出，內部產生資金仍足以償付債務。流動比率低於行業中位數，反映大量遞延收入及其他流動負債，而非流動性壓力，此為我們的判斷。

overall_credit_view.text: 我們認為信貸狀況強勁，受到淨現金、穩健自由現金流及低於行業中位數的槓桿支持。指示性財務風險狀況為最低。營運利潤率落後行業中位數，營運收入較上年下降，故盈利能力趨勢值得監察，即使收入增長快於行業。
我們的前瞻觀點是債務償付能力仍然充裕，自由現金流及現金結餘覆蓋可換股票據。收購及回購消耗大部分自由現金流，而可換股票據到期時間未披露。我們將監察再融資計劃及盈利能力復甦；指示性狀況並非評級。
